notes: Changed the empty-string case: E6 shows `""` produces `"z"`, not `"y"`. The empty string has no final `y`, yet no `y` is appended — so the "append y" rule doesn't apply to empty input, and the observed output is just `"z"`. All other rules (first-char shift, no-append when input ends in `y`) are consistent with E1–E6.
